column3: Both slaughtering verbs have active plural subjects; the sprinkling subject is singular and unnamed.
Presentation has an active singular subject rather than a passive construction.
Removal has an active singular subject rather than a passive construction.
The hide belongs explicitly “to the priest, to him,” repeating the recipient.
“Each like his brother” retains the family expression behind equal portions.
Oil is named without specifying olive oil.
The final prohibition has an active singular subject rather than a passive construction.
The Hebrew says “the meat” without explicitly adding “other.”
The Hebrew says any work without explicitly adding “other.”
His hands are the grammatical subject of bringing.
